issue.title: Review is an obligation with an artifact: fr journal check --require-reviews (gh-430)

repository.name: super-fr
repository.description: Claude Code plugin suite: superpowers-wrapped planning, devcontainer+worktree isolation, goal-to-PR autonomy, and phase dispatch to VibeKanban runners

issue.body:
Closes #430.

## What this does

Per-phase code review was the only fr-goal obligation with no enforcing artifact. Nothing recorded that a review happened, and nothing noticed when one didn't — so "review skipped" and "review passed clean" were the same state, and an obligation whose satisfaction and violation look identical is not a control.

Three pieces:

1. **An artifact.** A reviewed phase writes a plan-journal entry with `kind=review` and `phase=N`. No schema change — `review` was already a `JournalKind` and `phase` already an optional field, so no stamp bump and no migration are owed.
2. **A gate.** `fr journal check --require-reviews` fails when a phase the plan claims is done has no review entry naming it. Opt-in; without the flag, behaviour is byte-identical to before.
3. **A call site that isn't prose.** A `kind: cli` step `journal-check` in the shipped `fr-goal` manifest, between `implement` and `deliver`, whose exit code is the verdict. #430's own thesis applied to its fix: an obligation enforced by an instruction can be absorbed.

Plus the skill prose that emits the entry (fr-goal §6, fr-debugging), and the published explainer, which narrates this pipeline and so is owed under `.claude/rules/explainers-currency.md`.

- Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-20-journal-require-reviews-design.md`
- Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-20-journal-require-reviews/`

## It was dogfooded on itself

The gate ran against its own plan, in both states, on the real artifact rather than a fixture:

```
# phase 2 complete, not yet reviewed
$ fr journal check --scope plan --plan-dir docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-20-journal-require-reviews --require-reviews
1 phase(s) owed a review, none recorded: 2
  fr journal add --scope plan --slug 2026-09-20-journal-require-reviews --kind review --phase 2 ...
(manual phases are exempt from --require-reviews — spec D4)
exit=1

# after the review entry was written
exit=0
```

and then as a real cursor step on this PR's own run:

```
$ fr run advance 2026-09-20-journal-require-reviews-v2
journal-check: done (exit 0)
```

## Two design points worth reading

**The completion predicate.** #430 says "a phase has `completion.at` set". `fr/render.py` carries two predicates and the obvious one is wrong: `_phase_complete` requires an *observed merged PR* for agentic phases, and fr-goal opens its only PR at `deliver` — after this gate. A gate built on it would have passed every plan forever while looking healthy. It uses `plan_locally_complete` (`completion.at` set **or** every step ticked), which is deliberately wider than asked: a phase with every step ticked and no `completion.at` still claims to be done and must not be an escape hatch.

**Opt-in, not default-on.** Of this repo's 13 plan-scope `review` entries, only 8 carry a `phase=` token, so a default-on gate would fail live and archived plans over a convention never stated. The flag's weakness — someone must remember it — is closed by the manifest step passing it, not by breaking consumers.

## Review

Six phases, six reviews, 24 findings: 23 fixed, 1 refuted. Phases 1–3 were reviewed by independent subagents with no session context; 4–6 inline, where the defects were found by *running* the documented commands and by word-level diffs. Every fix was mutation-verified — several of my own first attempts asserted nothing and were rewritten.

The ones that mattered:

- **`r-p1-f1`** — `--plan-dir .` derived an empty slug, resolved a journal that doesn't exist, read it as empty, and exited **0 having checked nothing**, including the open-findings rule that predates this PR. Verified live: the same journal by `--slug` exited 1 with four open findings.
- **`r-p2-f1`** — a plan parsing to zero phases exited 0 having evaluated nothing. The realistic trigger is a phase file misnamed `1.yaml`, which `fr.parser` drops silently, so a plan with a real, complete, unreviewed phase sailed through green.
- **`r-p3-f1`** — CI proved the cursor *reached* the gate, never that it *blocked*. The composed promise of this whole PR was asserted nowhere. Now pinned by an integration test that ticks a phase's step, asserts `fr run advance` fails with the cursor unmoved and `deliver` pending, then adds the review entry and asserts the run proceeds. That is **spec Test Plan item 4, promoted from post-merge into CI**.
- **`r-p3-f3`** — the shipped manifest called this step a "backstop … not a duplicate" of the per-phase loop. The loop enforces nothing: `review-phase` is `kind: agent` and completes on `resolve`, so a skipped review resolves identically to a performed one. That prose ships to consumers and would justify deleting the step.
- **`r-p4-f1`** and **`r-p6-f2`** — twice, this PR documented a command that does not work: `fr journal add --kind review --state done` (exits 2; `state` is only valid on `finding` entries), and the drift recovery `fr run adopt <plan-dir> --run-id <fresh>` (refuses while the stranded run file exists — precisely the case it is for). Both were found by running them. Both are this PR's own failure class, inside the PR.

Full text: `fr journal render --scope plan --slug 2026-09-20-journal-require-reviews --section findings`.

## Known gaps, stated rather than discovered

- **No gate runs or parses a command a skill documents.** `r-p4-f1` shipped a broken one through canonical source and two mirror sets with everything green. A tripwire is buildable but needs a placeholder convention first (`<s>`, `<f>`, `N`) — recorded as `d-p4-no-tripwire-runs-skill-commands`, not built here.
- **`fr run adopt` semantics.** Recovery from this step's drift needs the stranded run file moved aside first; adoption then re-dispatches `review-phase` for every completed phase, and does not carry the old cursor's gate provenance. All three confirmed by running it. The prose now says so; changing `adopt` belongs in its own spec.
- **The 120-line skill cap was paid for by joining lines**, which hides deletions inside re-flowed paragraphs. Exactly one word (`deterministic`) was lost and restored; a word-level diff is how that was established, and is the check worth repeating.
- **The gate does not judge review quality.** A review entry saying "no findings" satisfies it, exactly as `fr journal check` is satisfied by a finding marked `refuted`. The explainer states this limit plainly rather than implying it away.

## Verification

```
$ uv run pytest
3 failed, 3319 passed, 80 skipped in 209.15s
Required test coverage of 75% reached. Total coverage: 91.71%
```

The three failures are pre-existing and unrelated, re-confirmed on this branch: the only source files it changes under `packages/` are `commands/journal_cmd.py` and `journal/model.py`, while `run/workspace.py` is byte-identical to `origin/main`. Two are `test_run_workspace.py` assertions that depend on a Rich wrap point this machine's long `pytest` tmp path pushes into the asserted substring; the third is `test_workflow_check.py::test_cli_all_fails_when_nothing_is_discoverable` (#463/#489).

`ruff check` clean, `ruff format` clean, `mypy` clean over 138 source files, `bump-version.py --check` ok, `fr acceptance check` 127 rows OK, `fr validate artifacts` 33 artifacts valid.

## Operator gates

Verbatim from `fr run gates 2026-09-20-journal-require-reviews-v2`:

```
brainstorm: cleared, but provenance not recorded (this cursor predates `answered_by`)
```

To be accurate about that line: the **original** run recorded `--answered-by operator` for the batched Q&A, which the operator did answer — all four questions, with the recommended option chosen each time (logged as spec-scope decisions `d1`–`d4`). The provenance was lost when phase 3's deliberate step-drift forced a `fr run adopt`, which does not carry it. That is `r-p6-f2`'s third confirmed cost, not an unasked gate.

## Acceptance

Three rows, all added with this spec and all now `ci`:

- `journal-require-reviews-gate` — the gate's full behaviour, evidenced by `tests/unit/test_journal_cmd.py`.
- `journal-review-entry-per-phase` — the machine-readable trace, evidenced by `test_journal_model.py::TestReviewedPhases`. Deliberately **not** also citing the integration test: that is the third row's claim, and citing it here would repeat `r-p3-f2`, where a row was flipped on evidence covering half its acceptance.
- `fr-goal-review-gate-is-cursor-enforced` — placement by `test_tripwire_shipped_workflows.py`, and the "cannot reach the PR step" clause by the new blocking integration test.

`fr acceptance check`: 127 rows OK (ci 105, skipped 18, not-implemented 4). The warnings it prints are pre-existing archived-spec path moves in unrelated rows.

## Test Plan

Verbatim from the spec — **post-merge, operator-driven**:

1. On a live plan, mark a non-manual phase complete (by `completion.at` or by ticking every step) with no `review` entry naming it; confirm `fr journal check --scope plan --plan-dir <dir> --require-reviews` exits 1 and names that phase.
2. Emit the entry with `fr journal add --kind review --phase N`; confirm the same command exits 0.
3. Confirm a `[manual]` phase with `completion.at` set does **not** appear in the failure list, and that the message says why.
4. On a real fr-goal run, confirm `fr run advance` executes the `journal-check` step and blocks `deliver` on its non-zero exit.
5. Confirm a run started against the pre-change shape reports drift naming `added: journal-check`, and that the recovery works.

Items 1–5 were all exercised during this run; 4 is additionally now pinned in CI. They remain here because the spec listed them as operator-driven and the operator should see them run on their own plans.

## Version

Minor: **4.8.0 → 4.9.0** — a new CLI flag plus a new mandatory workflow step is a user-visible workflow addition. The bump arrived uncommitted in the worktree from an earlier session; it was **verified** (version-only diff across all ten surfaces, `bump-version.py --check` ok, `fr --version` 4.9.0) rather than re-made, because re-running `bump-version.py minor` from that state would have landed 4.10.0.

---

## Ready checklist — do not mark ready until all three hold

- [ ] CI green on this branch
- [ ] Explicit review OK from the operator
- [ ] No commits pushed since that OK

issue.title: fr-goal stops mid-run with nothing blocking it: "keep going" is an obligation with no enforcing artifact

repository.name: super-fr
repository.description: Claude Code plugin suite: superpowers-wrapped planning, devcontainer+worktree isolation, goal-to-PR autonomy, and phase dispatch to VibeKanban runners

issue.body:
Split out of the gh-430 run (#517), where it was observed twice in one session. This is the same defect shape as #430 — an obligation with no enforcing artifact — but aimed at the orchestrator's **liveness** rather than its reviews.

## Observed

During the #430 run, `/fr-goal` stopped and handed back to the operator **twice** with nothing blocking it: once after phase 1's review-and-fix completed, once after phase 2's. The operator reported it as the third occurrence that day across sessions, and named it: *"this smells like a systemic error."*

Neither stop was a legitimate touchpoint. `fr-goal`'s SKILL.md enumerates exactly three — the batched Q&A (`gate: operator`), manual phases, and the PR merge — and none applied. In both cases the run cursor was ready: `fr run advance` would have printed the next phase's dispatch brief immediately.

## Why it happens

Three pressures compound, and none of them is the agent deciding to stop:

1. **The loop's cadence ends on a report.** §5/§6 is dispatch → return → review → fix → push. Every iteration terminates in a subagent hand-back, which arrives *as a message*. Replying to a delivered report by summarising it is the default conversational move; dispatching the next agent **and** reporting in the same turn is the less natural one. The harness shape rewards the wrong reflex.
2. **Review-fix work is done inline by the orchestrator**, not delegated. So each iteration ends with it personally holding a pile of findings it just fixed — maximum reporting pressure at exactly the point the skill wants zero pause.
3. **Output style competes with the skill's contract.** That session ran in `explanatory` style, which instructs surfacing educational insight as work proceeds. A skill's autonomy contract should outrank an output-style preference; there is nothing making it do so.

## The structural point

**"Keep going" is an fr-goal obligation with no enforcing artifact.**

The run cursor already holds the state — it knows the next step, and `fr run advance` emits it on demand. But nothing consults it before a turn ends, and nothing records that a turn ended mid-run. A run that stalled and a run that is working look identical from outside until a human notices the wall clock.

That is #430's sentence with one word changed: *there is no state in which "stopped mid-run" is distinguishable from "still working."* And it is doubly awkward for the same reason #430 was — the machinery to answer the question is already present and already invoked; it just produces no signal.

## Proposed

Deliberately not prescribing the fix, since the right answer depends on how much the harness can be relied on to re-invoke.

1. **Make the state legible.** `fr run status` already knows the cursor; it does not know *when* the step entered its current state. A `since` timestamp on `StepRecord` would let `fr run status` say `implement-phase phase/3: running since 14:22 (38m)`, which is the minimum needed for anything else here to be buildable. Note this is an artifact shape change and so owes a stamp bump + migration + validator under `.claude/rules/artifact-versioning.md`.
2. **Make the skill consult it.** fr-goal §5's loop could be required to end every turn either with a dispatched agent in flight or at one of the three named touchpoints — and to say which. Prose, but prose with a checkable referent, which is more than exists now.
3. **Consider a liveness signal.** Something like `fr run status --stalled` exiting non-zero when the cursor has been `running` with no in-flight work. Whether that is reachable depends on whether fr can observe in-flight dispatches at all, which today it cannot — worth establishing before designing around it.

Option 1 is the load-bearing one: without a timestamp, neither 2 nor 3 has anything to key on.

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

The #430 run found the same pattern three times in its own artifacts — a check that existed, was invoked, and produced no distinguishable state. An outside review absorbed into the working context (#430). A gate whose CI proved it *ran* but never that it *blocked* (`r-p3-f1` in #517). A documented recovery command that refused in exactly the case it was written for (`r-p6-f2`). Each was found only by someone asking a question nobody was required to ask.

This is the fourth instance, and the actor it concerns is the orchestrator — which is, as #430 put it, exactly the actor with no supervisor.

issue.title: One record per unit: who holds a phase, what it cost, was it reviewed, is anyone working (gh-503)

repository.name: super-fr
repository.description: Claude Code plugin suite: superpowers-wrapped planning, devcontainer+worktree isolation, goal-to-PR autonomy, and phase dispatch to VibeKanban runners

issue.body:
Closes #503. Closes #499. Closes #496. Closes #500. Closes #501. Closes #430. Closes #518.

> **Draft — do not merge yet.** See the Ready checklist at the bottom.

## What this PR became, and why

It began as #503 — *"nothing records which agent holds a phase."* It now carries **two specs, two
plans (13 phases), three folded-in branches and seven issues**, because on 2026-09-20 five
sessions worked one seam in parallel — *what the orchestrator intends versus what actually
happened to a dispatched unit* — and gave it five specs. The cost of that split is recorded in the
second spec's §1 and §8: two discarded implementations, **two different `schema_version: 3`s of
the same artifact**, two refusals for one issue, and a live data-loss bug. The operator's call was
to land the seam whole.

| folded in | what it carried | state |
|---|---|---|
| gh#519 `fix/fr-run-cursor-cluster` | #496 manual phases, a second #499 refusal, #500 session binding, #501 composite ids | merged `228d784`, PR closed as superseded |
| gh#517 `feat/journal-require-reviews` | #430 `fr journal check --require-reviews` | merged `85b1c92`, PR closed as superseded |
| `main` ×2 | gh#506 (tier ingestion — which had independently fixed two of this PR's own findings), gh#514 (telemetry, handoff bounds) | merged |

## The investigation #503 asked for

Eight `fr-phase-executor`s were dispatched; ten hours later the harness listed two, one of them
long since returned and still resumable with no worktree. **Nothing about the dispatch differed,
and nothing was reaped.** All eight are still fully recorded on disk, identical in dispatch shape.
The listing is a view over agents that are *not yet terminal*.

One never became terminal. Claude Code moves a foreground `Bash` call past its **120-second
timeout** into a background child; five of eight executors were promoted that way, none by choice.
One of them left behind an `until grep … ; do sleep 3; done` loop watching a file for a pattern
that never appeared. It ran **11.5 hours**. One live background child is the whole asymmetry —
neither the devcontainer nor fr-isolation is implicated — and killing the child did *not* retire
the agent, which is why a holder record needs its own explicit close.

## What ships

**One record per unit.** `StepRecord.units` replaces `items`, `dispatch` and top-level
`accounting`. Each unit holds its **attempts**, oldest first; each attempt carries who held it,
which session dispatched it, what it was estimated to cost and what it measurably burned.

| surface | behaviour |
|---|---|
| `fr run advance` | opens an attempt; **refuses** a held unit (exit 2, no brief, names the holder); `--redispatch` is the escape |
| `fr run claim` | **new** — records the reported agent id; `--abandoned` closes an attempt without resolving its step |
| `fr run resolve` | closes the attempt and measures it; a `review-phase` unit **refuses `done` without `--evidence review=<journal-entry-id>`** |
| `fr run status` | per attempt: holder, then estimate, then measurement — labelled as different quantities |
| `fr run check` | open and unclaimed dispatches, pre-gate reviews as debt; **`--idle` exits 3** on an advanceable run nobody is working; `--stalled-after` reports, never fails |
| Stop hook (Claude Code) | blocks ending a turn on an idle run and names the next command; silent for every legitimate stop; fail-open; once per cursor position |
| OpenCode plugin | continues the session on `session.idle` — weaker than blocking, and declared `partial` |
| `run` artifact | **v2 → v5** across this PR; the last hop is the first *body-rewriting* run migration |

`fr` cannot verify any *reported* field — the orchestrator says which agent it dispatched, exactly
as `--answered-by operator` says a human answered. Visibility, not enforcement.

### Verified on the run that built it

```
phase/3/implement-phase: done
  agent a6003d67… (claude-code, claude-fable-5-1) 21:04:30 -> 22:02:04 done
    ~23,599 tok est
    measured: 56,092,764 tok billed across the dispatch's turns
```

Identity and cost on one attempt — the split #464 and #503 had left between them. The evidence
gate was verified *by meeting it*: no evidence → exit 2; a `finding` id → exit 2; another phase's
review → exit 2; this phase's own → `done`, with the cursor byte-identical after the refusals. The
cursor migrated v4 → v5 **while holding an open attempt**: held before, held and still named after.

## Findings — 25 across two plan journals, none open

`fr journal render --scope plan --slug 2026-09-20-dispatch-holder-identity --section findings`
`fr journal render --scope plan --slug 2026-09-20-unit-record-unification --section findings`

Nearly every one is the same shape — **a claim that outran the code**:

| | the claim | the reality |
|---|---|---|
| f2 | the validator item had passing tests | it produced no code; two open records for one unit parsed cleanly |
| f3 | the notification said `exit code 0` | the suite was red — a pipeline exits with `tail`'s status |
| f4 + f6 | `model` = "the resolved tier binding" | `from_phase` is a sentinel **and** `fr plan create` silently dropped every `tier:` — `null` on every real dispatch (gh#506 fixed both independently, and better; its code is what ships) |
| f7 | `dispatch` held the holder history | `_complete_step` deleted a grouped step's whole map the moment it finished |
| f11 | three tests asserted a concrete `model` | reading the harness from the ambient machine — green here, red on CI |
| f13 | `run` was at `schema_version: 3` | so was gh#514's branch, for a different shape; nothing detects two branches allocating one number |
| f-p2-blind-grep | the plan's exit-criterion grep passed | `git grep -E` has no `\b`; it could not match anything, so it could not fail |
| p3 | synthesized attempts + "held iff last attempt open" | **jointly wrong**: every pre-#508 unit of every migrated cursor read as HELD |

**Executors refuted the orchestrator's spec four times, with evidence, and were upheld each
time** — the synthesized-attempt hold above (30 synthesized attempts on real captures, zero wrongly
held after the fix); "a `phase/<n>` key is always `manual`" (a captured v1 cursor says otherwise);
a second design conflict between gh#508 and gh#519 the orchestrator had not listed; and two facts
only the Claude Code binary could supply (`background_tasks`, and a built-in cap on Stop-hook blocks).

A recurring sub-theme, fixed each time and now in shipped guidance: **a verification that cannot
fail is not one.** A masked exit code, an inert `set -e`, a grep that matches nothing, a mutation
that never applied, a `$` that was an anchor — every one read as a pass. Mutation checks now print
whether they applied, and the new tripwire carries its own positive control.

## Operator gates

Run `2026-09-20-feat-phase-holder-identity` (captured before its cursor drifted — gh#517's new
`journal-check` step means `fr run gates` now refuses this completed run, by design):

```
brainstorm: operator gate answered by the operator
```

Run `2026-09-20-unit-record-unification-r2`, verbatim:

```
brainstorm: cleared, but provenance not recorded (this cursor predates `answered_by`)
```

That second line is an artefact of **adoption**, which cannot carry provenance; the wording
("predates") is not quite the truth. For the record: the operator answered four question batches
for that spec (nine questions — scope, the gh#519 fold-in, and decisions `u1`–`u5`), reviewed the spec
over four rounds, and approved the plan. Its first cursor was stranded by manifest drift mid-run and
re-adopted; the dispatch history lost in that recovery is preserved in the plan journal.

## Operator review — two comments, both acted on

**"is this valid yaml?"** (a cursor's `stdout: 'self-review passed` folded over three lines).
Valid — three ways — but it looked broken, and a failed step's output rendered as one escaped
blob. `fr.run.model.dump_cursor_yaml` is now the ONE cursor writer; multi-line strings are block
literals, round trip exact (18 awkward strings pinned), no schema change. Widening the
writer-agreement test to every captured cursor then found something nobody asked about: the
4→5 rewrite ordered `synthesized` ahead of the cost fields, so **every migrated cursor would
have reordered itself on its first native save.** Fixed in `v4_to_v5`, mutation-checked.

**"I would expect another element here, invoking `superpowers:receiving-code-review`. Is it
being left at the implementing agent's discretion?"** It was — and this run proves it: every
phase was reviewed inline, with neither review skill invoked through the harness. Decision
`u6` (spec §4.E.1): `skill:` takes an ordered list and the member names both; and
`evidence: [review, findings]`, where **`findings` is derived, never passed** — `resolve
--state done` refuses while any finding filed against that phase is still open, prints the
`fr journal resolve` line for each, and records the ids it saw closed. Deferral is a phase
number, not a new state. Deliberately **not** a third member step: drift compares member ids,
and a new one strands every `fr-goal` cursor in flight. Five mutations each fail the suite;
disabling the gate fails the shipped-shape walk. **Limit:** it enforces that findings *end
closed*, not that the review was rigorous or a refutation well reasoned.

## Acceptance

**36 rows added since `origin/main`** (the 36th, `run-review-findings-gate`, by the operator review below), grouped in the second spec's §7 by what could go wrong:
upgrade safety, the witness, cost, evidence, liveness. Repo total: `ci: 146, skipped: 18,
not-implemented: 7`. Three rows of this PR stay `not-implemented` **on purpose** — each is
live-only by nature:

- `run-dispatch-harness-neutral` — two different harnesses writing one record shape; a fixture
  only shows that fr writes what fr writes.
- `run-pickup-on-another-host` — its unit half landed; its claim is two real machines.
- `run-idle-reprompt-opencode` — all 50 `bun` tests drive a fake client.

gh#519's `run-advance-refuses-running` is merged into `run-dispatch-refuses-second` by notes on
both rows (there is no delete verb); both stay `ci`.

## Limits and costs, stated

- **The idle guard only reaches session-bound runs**, calls the `fr` on PATH (a stale global `fr`
  exits 2 and *silently disables it*), and adds ~2 s to each turn end of a bound session.
- **Hermes has no adapter** — there, fr-goal's prose is all there is. OpenCode's is `partial`.
  Codex and Copilot CLI are `unsupported` across the matrix; their block-capable stop hooks are
  noted as leads, unverified except that Copilot CLI's hooks system is installed.
- **Not exercised:** the Stop hook delivered through a plugin's `hooks.json`, `background_tasks`
  while a subagent really runs, interactive sessions — Test Plan item 17. The plugin's TypeScript
  is tested (`bun test`) but was not type-checked.
- **Known wrinkle, not fixed here:** session bindings say `harness: "claude"` where `fr.harness`
  says `"claude-code"`. The guard keys on `worktree` only.

## On upgrade

Only the `run` kind moves. A cursor migrates at the first `fr` command (an agent runs
`fr migrate artifacts --yes` itself — standing behaviour). Held units stay held and named; recorded
cost moves onto the last attempt; cost older than the dispatch record gets a **synthesized**
attempt that is never a hold. Reviews resolved before the evidence gate read `done, unevidenced` —
debt, never a failure — while reviews still to come need evidence. A cursor that cannot be
converted is left byte-identical. Everything under `implemented/` stays frozen; the new frozen
legacy reader can still parse an archived cursor on demand.

## Verification

Full suite as CI sees it (`CLAUDE*` unset): **3966 passed, 80 skipped, 0 failed**, coverage
**92.21%**. `ruff format --check`, `ruff check`, `mypy` (146 files), `bump-version --check`
(**4.12.0**), `fr acceptance check` + `report --check`, `fr validate artifacts` (48),
`fr harness parity --check`, both mirror generators, `fr workflow check fr-goal`,
`fr journal check --require-reviews` on both plans, `bun test` (50) — all clean. Explainer
renderer verified byte-identical on the unmodified source before the real render.

## Test Plan — post-merge, operator-driven

**Post-merge, operator-driven (decision d4) — both harnesses:**

13. A live `/fr-goal` run on **Claude Code**: `fr run status` during a phase shows that phase
    held by the real subagent id, and after it returns shows the dispatched→returned pair with
    `harness: claude-code` and the tier's model. Transcript in the PR.
14. The same on **OpenCode**, recording `harness: opencode` and the child session id, proving
    the record is harness-neutral rather than Claude-shaped.
15. On one of those runs, deliberately `advance` twice for the same phase and confirm the
    refusal fires with the real holder id — the #499 behaviour, live.

**Post-merge, operator-driven** (extends #508's items 13–15):

16. On the live Claude Code run of item 13: `fr run status` shows cost **under each
    attempt**, and after a deliberate `claim --abandoned` + re-dispatch, both attempts'
    costs are present.
17. End a turn mid-run with the run idle: the Stop hook blocks and names `fr run advance`.
    End one while an executor works: it does not.
18. Try to resolve a `review-phase` unit `done` with no review entry: refused.
## Process finding — recorded, not designed

Five sessions, one seam, no shared view. Two cheap guards would have prevented most of this PR's
reconciliation work: **batch issues that name the same structure into one spec**, and a
**registry-side check that two open branches have not allocated the same artifact version**.
Neither is built here; both are why the second spec exists.

---

**Ready checklist — this PR is a DRAFT until all three hold.** Do not merge before:

- [ ] CI green on this branch
- [ ] Explicit review approval
- [ ] No commits pushed since that approval
